chats.answer:
Yes! You can turn a Blink or Wyze camera you already own into a DIY bird feeder camera without paying a monthly subscription.

The main difference is how each brand handles recording.

My recommendation: Use Wyze if you have both. Wyze generally offers more flexibility for recording birds locally, while Blink can work well for motion-triggered bird videos.

You don't need to buy a dedicated bird feeder camera. You can mount your existing camera near a regular bird feeder, adjust the viewing angle, and use its motion detection to capture visiting birds.

Wyze confirms that cameras with microSD slots support subscription-free local recording. Blink supports subscription-free clips through a Sync Module 2 with USB storage or a compatible XR module with microSD storage. 
Wyze
+2

How I'd build it

Attach a regular bird feeder to a post, railing, or tree-mounted bracket.

Mount your camera nearby, pointing toward the feeding perch.

Test the focus distance before permanently attaching it. Many security cameras aren't designed for extreme close-ups.

Set motion detection to focus on the feeder, reducing false alerts from moving branches.

Enable local recording so you can review visits without a subscription.

For a Wyze camera with a microSD slot, choose Continuous or Events Only under local recording settings. 
Wyze

One limitation: Neither camera automatically provides the same bird-species identification features as some dedicated smart bird feeders. You can still save photos and identify the birds separately.
